subject: Notice ladder, grace triggers, and Termination-for-Convenience (TFC) alignment
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@rivalcorp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: liam.oneill@rivalcorp.com
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Renewal notice window & TFC question

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked solid. Legal has a couple of asks on the MSA/order form we need to resolve before procurement can put the PO on the queue: specifically around auto-renew timing and the termination-for-convenience (TFC) mechanics.

Short summary of Rival's position (from our counsel):
- We want a single 90-day written notice window for non-renewal (no staggered notices across product modules).
- If Rival terminates for convenience during an active term, we expect pro-rated credits and a 30-day data export window without additional fees.
- If Redwood terminates for convenience, Rival wants a 120-day wind-down to migrate and a right to refund for unused pre-paid committed capacity.

Two asks: can Redwood align to a single notice window (90 days) rather than module-level ladders, and can you confirm Redwood's position on TFC reciprocity and migration support?

I'm attaching a redline and a short concessions matrix. If easier, we can set a short call with legal this week.

Thanks,

Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, Rival Corp
maya@rivalcorp.com
attachments: [Redline: Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 128KB), Concessions: Rival_Concession_List.xlsx (xlsx, 32KB)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Maya Singh <maya@rivalcorp.com>
Cc: kArthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Renewal notice window & TFC question

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping Karthik (contracts) and Laura (legal ops) so we can get a single, consolidated response.

High-level thoughts before we sync:
- Single notice window: we prefer a product-level approach because some customers have multi-bundle add-ons that are independent, but we can be pragmatic. We can offer a single 90-day notice for the base MSA/order form as a contractual commitment if Rival is willing to accept the standard per-product breakpoints documented in the order form (i.e., the notice applies to the overall agreement, but specific add-on decommissions may have shorter technical lead times).
- TFC reciprocity: Redwood is open to reciprocal TFC but needs to preserve operational safety nets. We typically require a 60-day wind-down if Redwood initiates TFC to ensure customer data exports and transfer of KV caches; we can discuss extending to 120 days for larger committed customers with a phased migration plan.
- Refund mechanics: pro-rated refunds for prepaid committed capacity are acceptable for good-faith TFC, but we'd ask for an offset for any non-cancellable reserved capacity costs.

Propose: a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the redline and agree on 3 bullet-level compromises we can commit to in the MSA: single 90-day notice, reciprocal TFC with 120/60 wind-down ladder depending on the initiator, and explicit data export SLA on termination.

If that sounds right, I'll run a short internal quick-scan with Legal and Ops and come back with precise wording.

— Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference | Redwood Inference, Inc.

Subject: Redwood internal: Proposed wording and operational runbook for Rival TFC/renewal asks

Jonas — quick internal thread after reading Rival's redline. Summarized recommended approach below, plus the operational runbook we should push to Ops for feasibility.

Recommended contract language (high level):
1) Renewal/Notice: Agreement auto-renews for successive 1-year terms unless either party provides 90 days' prior written notice before the end of the applicable term. The notice applies at the agreement level and supersedes per-product module notice requirements, provided Redwood documents technical decommission timelines in the Order Form Schedule A.
2) Termination for Convenience (TFC): Each party may terminate for convenience with the following wind-down obligations:
   - If Customer (Rival) initiates TFC: Redwood will provide a 30-day data export window and provide pro-rata credits for unused pre-paid committed capacity within 45 days of termination.
   - If Redwood initiates TFC: Redwood will provide a 120-day wind-down period and reasonable migration assistance; pro-rated refunds for unused committed capacity will be paid within 60 days, subject to deduction for non-cancellable reserved capacity costs.
3) Operational SLA on data export: Redwood will provide an export package (export.tar.gz or S3 export manifest) within the designated data export window; failure entitles Customer to an additional 15 days of access at no charge.

Operational runbook (Ops required items):
- Prepare a templated Data Export package (small, medium, large) and service-level export checklist.
- Define reserved-capacity offset calculation and a published example.
- Provide a documented per-product technical decommission timeline to attach as Schedule A to any order form.
- Implement an internal flagging mechanism so legal/CS can request extended wind-downs for customers above $X TCV.

Edge cases / risks for sales to note:
- Pilot accounts with monthly billing: offering 120-day Redwood-initiated wind-down is operationally heavy; propose a capped 60-day exception for pilots.
- Customers with cross-region private deployments: data export logistics may require additional fees; flag to Solutions.

If you want, I'll draft precise redline language (tracked changes) and an Ops ticket for engineering to validate the export timelines. Laura — any red flags from legal ops? Aditya — can your team provide the reserve-capacity offset formula?

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Renewal notice window & TFC question

Jonas and team — appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed Karthik's proposed approach with counsel and procurement; overall that structure is workable for Rival with two small clarifications:

1) For Customer-initiated TFC (Rival): we need the data export window to be 45 days instead of 30, since our migration involves third-party integrators. If Redwood sees this as acceptable, we can sign-off.
2) For Redwood-initiated TFC: Rival requests the refund timing be 45 days instead of 60 to align with their own finance reconciliation cycles.

If you can accept those two tweaks (45 day export on customer TFC; 45 day refund on Redwood TFC), Rival will sign the MSA and we can route the PO. If Redwood needs the reserved-capacity deduction clause, please provide the published example calculation so procurement sign-off can proceed.

Happy to do a 15-minute call to finalize, otherwise we can exchange a one-page concession confirmation.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, Rival Corp
